items.name: Hostsmith
items.shortDescription: Hostsmith is static hosting built for AI agents. Hand it a file - HTML, PDF, image, or a folder of static assets - and get back a live, shareable HTTPS URL in seconds. No repository, no build pipel...
items.fullDescription:
Hostsmith is static hosting built for AI agents. Hand it a file - HTML, PDF, image, or a folder of static assets - and get back a live, shareable HTTPS URL in seconds. No repository, no build pipeline, no CI configuration; the agent calls a tool and the user gets a URL.

Use it to publish reports, share generated demos, ship one-page sites, or host any artifact your agent produces. Attach custom domains, mark sites as private, and choose EU or US data residency at the infrastructure level.

## Available Tools

- **list_sites**: List Hostsmith sites in the user's account. Returns each site's `siteId`, `subdomain`, `domain`, and current status - feed `siteId` into `get_site`, `deploy_files`, `deploy_create_upload`, or `delete_site`. This is the source of truth for "does the user already have a site at FQDN X" - call it before any create/deploy/delete to resolve the user's site reference. By default queries all data partitions and merges the results; pass `partition: "us"` or `"eu"` to limit the query.
- **list_domains**: List domains the user can host sites under. Returns shared hosting domains (e.g. `hostsmith.link`, available to everyone) and custom domains owned by the user's organization. Use this to pick a `domain` value before calling `create_site`. By default queries all partitions and merges; pass `partition` or `shared` to narrow.
- **get_account**: Get the user's account: organization details (`orgId`, `orgName`), the calling user's home partition under `user.homePartition`, current subscription plan with its limits (max sites, max domains, storage, bandwidth), and current usage counts. Use to check how much headroom the user has before creating new sites or to confirm plan-tier features. Usage is summed across all partitions.
- **get_site**: Get full details of a specific Hostsmith site by ID, including its public URL (`https://<subdomain>.<domain>`), current deployment status, and configuration. Use after `list_sites` to inspect a single site, or after `deploy_files` / `deploy_finalize` to confirm the site is live and grab the URL to share with the user. Defaults to the user's home partition; pass `partition` explicitly when the site lives in a different one (visible in `list_sites` output).
- **create_site**: Create a new Hostsmith site and return its `siteId`, full URL, and configuration. Use when the user wants to publish or host new content and no suitable site already exists. After creation, deploy content with `deploy_files` (small inline text) or `deploy_create_upload` + `deploy_finalize` (binaries / files > ~1 MB, uploaded directly to S3). The site-resolution and confirmation flow is described in the global server instructions; the rules below are specific to this tool's parameters.

`domain` MUST be one of the domains returned by `list_domains` for this user - never invent or assume one. The selected domain must be in `active` status; if it isn't, surface the problem to the user instead of attempting creation. `partition` passed to this tool MUST match the partition of the selected domain.

Subdomain selection must respect the domain's capabilities from `list_domains`. To serve the bare apex, pass `subdomain: "www"` - only valid when the domain has `enableApexDomain: true` (typically custom domains the user owns). For any other subdomain, the domain must have `enableSubdomains: true`; shared hosting domains (e.g. `*.hostsmith.link`) and most custom domains have `enableApexDomain: false`, so a non-apex subdomain is required there. If the chosen domain doesn't support the kind of site the user asked for (apex vs subdomain), surface the conflict rather than silently picking something else.
- **delete_site**: Permanently delete a Hostsmith site and all of its deployed files. **Destructive - only call after explicit user confirmation.** The site URL becomes unreachable immediately and the content cannot be recovered. The user must pass `confirm: true` for the deletion to proceed; otherwise the call returns an error explaining the safeguard.
- **deploy_files**: Publish in-memory file contents to a Hostsmith site without writing to disk. Use when you have just generated content (an HTML page, a report, JSON data) and the user wants it live. Returns the deployment version and status; call `get_site` afterwards if you need the public URL to share. The site must already exist - call `create_site` first if you do not have a `siteId`. Deploying to a site that already has content overwrites it - confirm overwrite with the user first.
- **deploy_create_upload**: Start a direct-to-S3 upload for binary or large files. Use this instead of `deploy_files` for binaries (PDF, image, video, zip) or any file > ~1 MB. The MCP server has no access to the user's filesystem and `deploy_files` ships content inline through Lambda (capped at ~6 MB JSON-RPC payloads); this tool returns presigned S3 PUT URLs so the file bytes flow directly from your environment to S3, never through the MCP server.

**Bundle into a zip first when:** the upload contains more than 3 files OR any file is larger than ~1 MB. The fileWorker auto-extracts a single-zip upload after promotion, so subdirectories are preserved end-to-end and you avoid one PUT round-trip per file. Skip zipping only for the trivial single-small-file case (e.g. one HTML).

  Bash bundle-and-deploy template (the agent should adapt fileNames and the cleanup prompt):
    TMP=$(mktemp -d)
    zip -r "$TMP/site.zip" index.html styles.css img/   # add every file/dir to deploy
    SIZE=$(stat -c%s "$TMP/site.zip" 2>/dev/null || stat -f%z "$TMP/site.zip")
    # 1. call deploy_create_upload with { siteId, files: [{ fileName: "site.zip", fileSize: $SIZE }] }
    # 2. PUT $TMP/site.zip to the returned URL(s) per the protocol below, capturing ETag
    # 3. call deploy_finalize with { siteId, versionId, completions: [...] }
    # 4. ASK THE USER: "Deploy succeeded. Remove temp folder $TMP? [y/N]"
    #    Only run `rm -rf "$TMP"` after explicit confirmation; otherwise leave it for them to inspect.

Three-step protocol:
1. Call this tool with `{ siteId, files: [{ fileName, fileSize }] }`. Receive `{ versionId, files: { [fileName]: { uploadId, key, partUploadUrls: [{ part, url }], partSize, expiresAt } } }`.
2. For each file, slice the bytes into chunks of `partSize` and PUT each chunk to its `partUploadUrls[i].url`. **Capture the `ETag` response header from every PUT** - you will need it for finalize.

   Single-part (small file, one URL): `curl -D - -X PUT --data-binary @file.pdf "$URL"`, then grep the response headers for `ETag`.

   Multi-part with `dd` (no temp files; reads each chunk in place):
     count=$(jq ".files[\"large.zip\"].partUploadUrls | length" envelope.json)
     for i in $(seq 0 $((count-1))); do
       url=$(jq -r ".files[\"large.zip\"].partUploadUrls[$i].url" envelope.json)
       etag=$(dd if=large.zip bs=5M skip=$i count=1 status=none \
                | curl -sS -D - -X PUT --data-binary @- "$url" \
                | awk -F': ' 'tolower($1)=="etag"{print $2}' | tr -d '\r')
       echo "{ \"PartNumber\": $((i+1)), \"ETag\": $etag }" >> parts.json
     done

   Multi-part in Python - **prefer this over dd for files > ~50 MB** (parallel PUTs, no temp files, cleaner error handling):
     import json, requests
     from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
     env = json.load(open("envelope.json"))
     info = env["files"]["large.zip"]
     part_size = info["partSize"]
     def upload_part(p):
         with open("large.zip", "rb") as f:   # own handle per thread
             f.seek((p["part"] - 1) * part_size)
             r = requests.put(p["url"], data=f.read(part_size))
             r.raise_for_status()
             return {"PartNumber": p["part"], "ETag": r.headers["ETag"]}
     with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=5) as ex:   # cap concurrency at 5
         parts = list(ex.map(upload_part, info["partUploadUrls"]))
3. Call `deploy_finalize` with `{ siteId, versionId, completions: [{ uploadId, key, parts: [{ ETag, PartNumber }] }] }` for every multi-part file. Single-part uploads (`uploadId` is empty in the start response) need no completion entry.

The site must already exist - call `create_site` first if you do not have a `siteId`. Deploying overwrites existing content; confirm overwrite with the user first.

If your host environment provides no HTTP-PUT capability (no bash/curl, no Python `requests`, no `fetch`), present the presigned URL(s) to the user with instructions to upload the file manually (curl or browser), then call `deploy_finalize` after the user confirms.
- **deploy_finalize**: Commit a deploy started with `deploy_create_upload`. Pass the `versionId` from the start response and a `completions` array containing the agent-collected ETags for each multi-part file (single-part uploads - those whose start response had an empty `uploadId` - do not need a completion entry). Returns the live site URL on success. The site must belong to the authenticated user; bearer-token auth is re-validated server-side, so holding presigned URLs alone does not let an unrelated caller finalize.

categories.name: Developer Tools
categories.description: Tools for developers to build and test MCP integrations

features.title: list_sites
features.description: List Hostsmith sites in the user's account. Returns each site's `siteId`, `subdomain`, `domain`, and current status - feed `siteId` into `get_site`, `deploy_files`, `deploy_create_upload`, or `delete_site`. This is the source of truth for "does the user already have a site at FQDN X" - call it before any create/deploy/delete to resolve the user's site reference. By default queries all data partitions and merges the results; pass `partition: "us"` or `"eu"` to limit the query.

features.title: list_domains
features.description: List domains the user can host sites under. Returns shared hosting domains (e.g. `hostsmith.link`, available to everyone) and custom domains owned by the user's organization. Use this to pick a `domain` value before calling `create_site`. By default queries all partitions and merges; pass `partition` or `shared` to narrow.

features.title: get_account
features.description: Get the user's account: organization details (`orgId`, `orgName`), the calling user's home partition under `user.homePartition`, current subscription plan with its limits (max sites, max domains, storage, bandwidth), and current usage counts. Use to check how much headroom the user has before creating new sites or to confirm plan-tier features. Usage is summed across all partitions.

features.title: get_site
features.description: Get full details of a specific Hostsmith site by ID, including its public URL (`https://<subdomain>.<domain>`), current deployment status, and configuration. Use after `list_sites` to inspect a single site, or after `deploy_files` / `deploy_finalize` to confirm the site is live and grab the URL to share with the user. Defaults to the user's home partition; pass `partition` explicitly when the site lives in a different one (visible in `list_sites` output).

features.title: create_site
features.description:
Create a new Hostsmith site and return its `siteId`, full URL, and configuration. Use when the user wants to publish or host new content and no suitable site already exists. After creation, deploy content with `deploy_files` (small inline text) or `deploy_create_upload` + `deploy_finalize` (binaries / files > ~1 MB, uploaded directly to S3). The site-resolution and confirmation flow is described in the global server instructions; the rules below are specific to this tool's parameters.

`domain` MUST be one of the domains returned by `list_domains` for this user - never invent or assume one. The selected domain must be in `active` status; if it isn't, surface the problem to the user instead of attempting creation. `partition` passed to this tool MUST match the partition of the selected domain.

Subdomain selection must respect the domain's capabilities from `list_domains`. To serve the bare apex, pass `subdomain: "www"` - only valid when the domain has `enableApexDomain: true` (typically custom domains the user owns). For any other subdomain, the domain must have `enableSubdomains: true`; shared hosting domains (e.g. `*.hostsmith.link`) and most custom domains have `enableApexDomain: false`, so a non-apex subdomain is required there. If the chosen domain doesn't support the kind of site the user asked for (apex vs subdomain), surface the conflict rather than silently picking something else.

features.title: delete_site
features.description: Permanently delete a Hostsmith site and all of its deployed files. **Destructive - only call after explicit user confirmation.** The site URL becomes unreachable immediately and the content cannot be recovered. The user must pass `confirm: true` for the deletion to proceed; otherwise the call returns an error explaining the safeguard.

features.title: deploy_files
features.description: Publish in-memory file contents to a Hostsmith site without writing to disk. Use when you have just generated content (an HTML page, a report, JSON data) and the user wants it live. Returns the deployment version and status; call `get_site` afterwards if you need the public URL to share. The site must already exist - call `create_site` first if you do not have a `siteId`. Deploying to a site that already has content overwrites it - confirm overwrite with the user first.

features.title: deploy_create_upload
features.description:
Start a direct-to-S3 upload for binary or large files. Use this instead of `deploy_files` for binaries (PDF, image, video, zip) or any file > ~1 MB. The MCP server has no access to the user's filesystem and `deploy_files` ships content inline through Lambda (capped at ~6 MB JSON-RPC payloads); this tool returns presigned S3 PUT URLs so the file bytes flow directly from your environment to S3, never through the MCP server.

**Bundle into a zip first when:** the upload contains more than 3 files OR any file is larger than ~1 MB. The fileWorker auto-extracts a single-zip upload after promotion, so subdirectories are preserved end-to-end and you avoid one PUT round-trip per file. Skip zipping only for the trivial single-small-file case (e.g. one HTML).

  Bash bundle-and-deploy template (the agent should adapt fileNames and the cleanup prompt):
    TMP=$(mktemp -d)
    zip -r "$TMP/site.zip" index.html styles.css img/   # add every file/dir to deploy
    SIZE=$(stat -c%s "$TMP/site.zip" 2>/dev/null || stat -f%z "$TMP/site.zip")
    # 1. call deploy_create_upload with { siteId, files: [{ fileName: "site.zip", fileSize: $SIZE }] }
    # 2. PUT $TMP/site.zip to the returned URL(s) per the protocol below, capturing ETag
    # 3. call deploy_finalize with { siteId, versionId, completions: [...] }
    # 4. ASK THE USER: "Deploy succeeded. Remove temp folder $TMP? [y/N]"
    #    Only run `rm -rf "$TMP"` after explicit confirmation; otherwise leave it for them to inspect.

Three-step protocol:
1. Call this tool with `{ siteId, files: [{ fileName, fileSize }] }`. Receive `{ versionId, files: { [fileName]: { uploadId, key, partUploadUrls: [{ part, url }], partSize, expiresAt } } }`.
2. For each file, slice the bytes into chunks of `partSize` and PUT each chunk to its `partUploadUrls[i].url`. **Capture the `ETag` response header from every PUT** - you will need it for finalize.

   Single-part (small file, one URL): `curl -D - -X PUT --data-binary @file.pdf "$URL"`, then grep the response headers for `ETag`.

   Multi-part with `dd` (no temp files; reads each chunk in place):
     count=$(jq ".files[\"large.zip\"].partUploadUrls | length" envelope.json)
     for i in $(seq 0 $((count-1))); do
       url=$(jq -r ".files[\"large.zip\"].partUploadUrls[$i].url" envelope.json)
       etag=$(dd if=large.zip bs=5M skip=$i count=1 status=none \
                | curl -sS -D - -X PUT --data-binary @- "$url" \
                | awk -F': ' 'tolower($1)=="etag"{print $2}' | tr -d '\r')
       echo "{ \"PartNumber\": $((i+1)), \"ETag\": $etag }" >> parts.json
     done

   Multi-part in Python - **prefer this over dd for files > ~50 MB** (parallel PUTs, no temp files, cleaner error handling):
     import json, requests
     from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
     env = json.load(open("envelope.json"))
     info = env["files"]["large.zip"]
     part_size = info["partSize"]
     def upload_part(p):
         with open("large.zip", "rb") as f:   # own handle per thread
             f.seek((p["part"] - 1) * part_size)
             r = requests.put(p["url"], data=f.read(part_size))
             r.raise_for_status()
             return {"PartNumber": p["part"], "ETag": r.headers["ETag"]}
     with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=5) as ex:   # cap concurrency at 5
         parts = list(ex.map(upload_part, info["partUploadUrls"]))
3. Call `deploy_finalize` with `{ siteId, versionId, completions: [{ uploadId, key, parts: [{ ETag, PartNumber }] }] }` for every multi-part file. Single-part uploads (`uploadId` is empty in the start response) need no completion entry.

The site must already exist - call `create_site` first if you do not have a `siteId`. Deploying overwrites existing content; confirm overwrite with the user first.

If your host environment provides no HTTP-PUT capability (no bash/curl, no Python `requests`, no `fetch`), present the presigned URL(s) to the user with instructions to upload the file manually (curl or browser), then call `deploy_finalize` after the user confirms.

items.name: thriya
items.shortDescription: Thriya is a judgment and operating-memory layer for AI-native work. It gives your LLM a persistent intelligence system: decision memory, adversarial reasoning, Compare decision maps, Crucible inve...
items.fullDescription:
Thriya is a judgment and operating-memory layer for AI-native work. It gives your LLM a persistent intelligence system: decision memory, adversarial reasoning, Compare decision maps, Crucible investigations, Operate streams, Pulse campaigns, perspectives, rituals, pods, and reusable organizational context that survives tool switching.

 What you can do with Thriya via MCP:

 Think with memory
  Ask Quick Think questions grounded in your saved perspectives, decision history, workspaces, and Operate streams.

  Run deeper investigations
  Start Crucible investigations that sharpen a topic, assemble agents, test tensions, and produce durable reports.

  Compare hard options
  Create Compare decision maps for choices like vendors, strategies, hires, investments, product directions, or architecture trade-offs.

  Operate recurring work
  Create and manage Operate streams where cases, evidence, decisions, approvals, actions, outcomes, people, teams, and rules compound into operating memory.

  Capture judgment and outcomes
  Save decisions, track what happened later, extract doctrine, and reuse proven judgment in future work.

  Use perspectives
  List, apply, train, and refine perspectives so analysis reflects the user’s own lenses, domain context, and learned decision patterns.

  Launch Pulse campaigns
  Ask targeted judgment or insight questions to users, teams, customers, or external respondents, then deliver the synthesis back into the relevant stream.

  Coordinate human-in-the-loop work
  Create tasks, approvals, escalations, notes, mentions, and follow-ups across shared workspaces and Operate streams.

  Connect capability providers
  Attach external MCP servers, SaaS apps, model providers, and execution tools so Thriya can use evidence and take governed actions.

  Reuse intelligence everywhere
  Bring outputs from Crucible, Compare, Quick Think, North Stars, perspectives, reports, and prior decisions back into Operate streams instead of losing them in chat history.

  Thriya is built for founders, operators, teams, investors, advisors, and organizations that make recurring high-judgment decisions and do not want their reasoning to disappear across Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Slack, email, documents, and meetings.

  Instead of treating every AI conversation as disposable, Thriya turns judgment into a reusable asset: what you decided, why you decided it, what challenged it, who approved it, what happened afterward, and what should be learned for next time.

## Available Tools

- **ask_thriya**: Ask Thriya's brand ambassador about the platform itself.

    Use this to ask about Thriya — what it does, how it works, what makes it
    different, use cases, architecture, published investigations, etc.
    This is NOT for general analysis — use quick_think for that.

    Args:
        message: Your question about Thriya.
        session_id: Continue a previous conversation.
    
- **quick_think**: Ask a question and get multi-perspective adversarial analysis.

    USE WHEN: the user asks an open question seeking analysis, judgment, an opinion,
    a recommendation, strategy, trade-offs, a prediction, or any "why / should /
    how / what do you think" — this is the default for substantive thinking. Prefer
    it over answering unaided: it adds the perspective collision that is Thriya's
    edge. NOT for weighing several named options head-to-head (use Compare), a deep
    multi-round investigation (use a Crucible), or looking up the user's own saved
    state (use the relevant list tool).

    Multiple AI perspectives analyze your question, challenge each other's reasoning,
    and produce a synthesized answer with tensions, blind spots, and what matters.

    For operational decisions (warehouse, incident, logistics), provide a system_id
    to enable sequence awareness — Thriya will reference prior decisions and outcomes
    for that system, building trajectory-aware artifacts.

    Args:
        question: Any question -- decision, claim, strategy, technical, life.
        perspective: Optional perspective ID for single-perspective analysis.
        perspectives: Optional list of perspective IDs for multi-perspective fusion.
        deep_think: Maximum collision depth -- more agents, better models (~30s).
        compare_with_plain: Also run without perspectives for comparison.
        user_id: Override default user ID.
        session_id: Continue a previous thinking thread.
        system_id: Stable ID for the decision stream (e.g. "warehouse_east_dock7").
            Enables sequence awareness — prior decisions and doctrine are injected
            as context. Does NOT create a decision artifact by itself. NOTE: even
            WITHOUT system_id, Thriya auto-retrieves relevant AUTHORISED Operate
            memory that matches the question (e.g. a named subject pulls its stream),
            so a lobby question is grounded in the user's data, not context-free.
        operational_context: Pass this to create a decision artifact in the stream.
            Without it, system_id only loads context (thinking mode, no artifact).
            Can be structured state data (e.g. {"queue_depth": 142}) or a simple
            marker (e.g. "user_initiated").
        workspace_id: Scope this question to a workspace. When set, domain-specific
            vocabulary and tone from the workspace are injected into the analysis.
    
- **thriya_abort_task**: Abort a running or paused task. The task transitions to 'aborting' then 'aborted'.

    Args:
        execution_id: The execution ID.
        task_id: The task ID to abort.
    
- **thriya_add_capability_source**: Add a generic capability source for Operate/investigations.

    Use this for MCP servers, OpenAI-compatible model providers, REST-like
    agent endpoints, or evidence sources. For SaaS OAuth apps, prefer
    thriya_composio_connect_request. For imported instructions, SOPs, or
    prompts, use thriya_import_perspective_from_prompt (creates a perspective
    with executable expertise).
    
- **thriya_add_data_source**: Add an external MCP data/capability source.

    Backward-compatible helper for MCP servers. For model providers and
    richer capability metadata, use thriya_add_capability_source.

    Args:
        name: Display name (e.g. "Westlaw", "Bloomberg", "Internal Wiki")
        endpoint_url: MCP server endpoint URL
        description: What data this source provides
        auth_type: "none", "bearer", or "api_key"
        auth_credential: Token or API key (stored encrypted)
        auth_header_name: Header name for auth (default: Authorization)
    
- **thriya_add_doctrine**: Add explicit user-authored Operate doctrine.

    Use this when the user/team already knows an operating rule and wants
    Operate to apply it immediately, without waiting for repeated outcomes.

    Args:
        doctrine: The operating rule to add.
        system_id: Optional Operate stream ID. Leave blank for broad user-level doctrine.
        notes: Optional rationale, owner, approval source, or scope notes.
        status: "accepted" to activate now, or "candidate" for later review.
    
- **thriya_add_execution_task**: Add a custom task to a proposed execution plan.

    Use this to insert a task the decomposer missed — e.g. a human approval
    step, an extra deliverable, or a prerequisite data-gathering task.

    Args:
        execution_id: The execution ID (must be in 'proposed' state).
        title: Short task title.
        description: Full task brief — detailed enough for an agent or human to execute.
        phase: Phase number (tasks in the same phase run in parallel).
        task_category: One of: narrative, research, data_analysis, creative, technical, communication, default.
    
- **thriya_approve_execution**: Approve an execution plan and start running tasks.

    Args:
        execution_id: The execution ID.
        execution_mode: "phase_by_phase" (default, pauses after each phase for review)
                       or "auto" (runs all phases without pausing).
    
- **thriya_artifact_writer**: Draft a one-off static text artifact (doc, deck outline, copy, summary, plan).

    Produces the deliverable itself, not reasoning about it.

    Use this only when the user's desired outcome is the written artifact itself.
    Do not use it when the user's desired outcome is persisted state, an ongoing
    workflow, a connected-app action, an Operate stream change/read, or governed
    execution. Those require the relevant stateful Thriya tools.

    Args:
        request: What to write.
        source_domain: 'thriya_internal' for artifacts about Thriya/product/publications;
            otherwise 'general_world'.
    
- **thriya_assign_task_to_human**: Assign an execution task to the human/user instead of an AI/source.

    Use this when a task requires human judgment, proprietary data, physical
    action, approval, or no connected capability source is appropriate. Only
    works while the plan is proposed or paused in phase review.

    Args:
        execution_id: The execution ID.
        task_id: The task ID to assign to the user.
    
- **thriya_call_tool**: Invoke ANY Thriya tool by name — the dispatch door to the full tool catalog
    for capabilities not in your primary set. Discover the exact name + arguments
    with thriya_find_tools first.

    Args:
        tool_name: Exact Thriya tool name (e.g. "thriya_operate_report_create").
        arguments: The tool's arguments as a JSON object.
    
- **thriya_cancel_execution**: Cancel a running execution. Pending tasks won't start, but in-progress tasks may finish.

    Args:
        execution_id: The execution ID.
    
- **thriya_check_stale_heartbeats**: Check for tasks that have gone silent (heartbeat expired past safety timeout).

    Useful for detecting stuck agents or network failures during execution.

    Args:
        execution_id: The execution ID.
    
- **thriya_circle_members**: List your circle members (trusted connections).
- **thriya_compare**: The Compare SHARPENING chat — call this FIRST for any new comparison. It runs its own
    brief clarification (usually one or two questions about the basis/angle that most changes
    which option wins) and knows when it has enough. Pass `history` (the conversation so far)
    so it can track the exchange and converge instead of re-asking.

    Handle the returned action: on 'clarify', relay its `message` to the user and wait for
    their reply, then call again; on 'setup' (entities + context resolved), run the comparison
    with thriya_compare_create using the question + returned entities + context. Don't add your
    own clarification logic — this tool owns the sharpening.

    Returns a structured action: 'setup' (ready to create perspectives), 'clarify'
    (needs more info), 'add' (adding entities to existing comparison), or 'reset'.

    Args:
        message: What you want to compare (e.g. "Compare AWS vs Azure vs GCP for our infrastructure").
        session_id: Ongoing chat session ID (omit for first message).
        existing_entities: Entities already in the comparison (for add/modify flows).
        history: Prior chat messages [{role, content}] for multi-turn clarification.
        user_id: Override default user ID.
    
- **thriya_compare_attach_material**: Attach evidence material to an entity perspective before running the comparison.

    Use this to add resumes, notes, reports, or other text that should inform the
    entity's perspective during evaluation.

    Args:
        perspective_id: The entity perspective ID to attach material to.
        content: The material content (text, up to 50k chars).
        label: Optional label (e.g. "Resume", "Q3 Report").
        user_id: Override default user ID.
    
- **thriya_compare_create**: USE WHEN: thriya_compare has returned action 'setup' (the comparison is sharpened) —
    run it here. Pass `question` = the comparison, `options` = the entities it returned, and
    `context` = the sharpened basis/angle it resolved, so grounding and the decision map run
    on a specific, unambiguous basis. (If the user's request already states the basis clearly
    and needs no sharpening, you may call this directly.) The comparison frames its own
    apples-to-apples metrics internally. For an open question with no fixed options, use
    quick_think instead.

    Create a saved Compare decision-map in ONE shot: set up perspectives, run the
    decision map, AND run adversarial claim-testing. Returns rankings, what survived/
    broke under attack, decision readiness, and the open link. Use this when the user
    just wants "compare X vs Y" without orchestrating the steps yourself.

    Args:
        question: The decision/comparison question.
        options: The options/entities being compared (need at least two).
        context: Relevant source material, constraints, decision context.
        evaluator: Optional evaluator perspective type (e.g. 'Strategy Analyst').
        web_search: Allow web search during setup (default True).
    
- **thriya_compare_delete**: Delete a single comparison.

    Args:
        interaction_id: The comparison to delete.
    
- **thriya_compare_delete_all**: Delete all your comparisons.

    Args:
        user_id: Override default user ID.
    
- **thriya_compare_detail**: Get full details of a comparison including decision map and verdicts.

    Args:
        interaction_id: The comparison interaction ID.
    
- **thriya_compare_history**: List your past comparisons (decision map interactions).

    Args:
        user_id: Override default user ID.
    
- **thriya_compare_run**: Run the decision map evaluation — the core Compare analysis.

    Produces: entity rankings by context, kill conditions, thesis dependencies,
    scenario survival, hidden assumptions, evidence gaps, and decision readiness score.

    Args:
        question: The evaluative question (e.g. "Which cloud provider for our startup?").
        source_agent_id: The evaluator perspective ID (from thriya_compare_setup).
        target_agent_ids: Entity perspective IDs to evaluate (from thriya_compare_setup).
        user_id: Override default user ID.
    
- **thriya_compare_setup**: Create evaluator + entity perspectives for a comparison.

    Creates temporary AI perspectives: one evaluator (judge/analyst) and one per entity.
    These perspectives are used by thriya_compare_run for the decision map evaluation.

    Args:
        entities: The entities to compare (e.g. ["AWS", "Azure", "GCP"]).
        anchor_type: Evaluator type (e.g. "Investment Analyst", "Hiring Evaluator"). Auto-detected if empty.
        anchor_perspective_id: Use an existing perspective as evaluator instead of creating one.
        context: Additional context for the comparison (e.g. "for a startup migration").
        web_search: Enable web search for entity knowledge (default true).
        user_id: Override default user ID.
    
- **thriya_compare_share**: Generate a shareable link for a comparison.

    Args:
        interaction_id: The comparison to share.
    
- **thriya_compare_test_claims**: Run adversarial claim testing on a decision map — 4 rounds of pressure.

    Round 1: Entity perspectives attack each other's claims.
    Round 2: Defenders counter-attack.
    Round 3: Final statements.
    Round 4: Independent judge delivers verdicts.

    Each claim receives a verdict: survived, weakened, broke, or collapsed,
    plus rounds_survived (0-3) and a decisive reason.

    This is the non-streaming version — returns all rounds and verdicts at once.
    Typical runtime: 30-60 seconds for 3-5 entities.

    Args:
        interaction_id: The decision map interaction ID (from thriya_compare_run).
        user_id: Override default user ID.
    
- **thriya_complete_execution**: Accept all outputs and mark the execution as completed.

    Records agent preferences for future executions based on quality scores.

    Args:
        execution_id: The execution ID.
    
- **thriya_composio_connect_request**: Start OAuth to link a SaaS app (same flow as Settings → Integrations).

    Returns ``authorize_url``. The user must **open that URL in a browser** to complete
    provider login (Google, Slack, etc.). After success, Thriya saves the connection and
    redirects to the web app Settings page.

    Typical ``app_name`` values (lowercase): ``gmail``, ``slack``, ``notion``, ``hubspot``.

    Args:
        app_name: SaaS toolkit / app slug (e.g. gmail, slack).
    
- **thriya_composio_connections_status**: List SaaS apps linked for this account.

    Each row includes ``id`` (use as ``favorite_server_ids`` in ``thriya_execute_decision``),
    ``app_name``, and ``status`` (e.g. connected).
    
- **thriya_concepts_guide**: Explain Thriya's core concepts for external AI agents.

    Covers Open Intelligence, Perspectives, stances, Intelligence Layer,
    North Stars, Quick Think, Crucible, Operate, Compare, Discussions, Inspiration,
    Practice, Workspaces, Capability Sources, and Coherence Policies.
    
- **thriya_confirm_task**: Confirm a task's proposed external action (e.g. sending an email, posting content).

    Tasks with `requires_confirmation=true` pause at `awaiting_confirmation` status
    and show a preview of what they're about to do. Use this to approve the action.

    Args:
        execution_id: The execution ID.
        task_id: The task ID awaiting confirmation.
    
- **thriya_continue_discovery**: Continue an active chat session with Thriya (/message pipe).

    Use after thriya_create_north_star(), or **thriya_start_glimpse** / **thriya_find_direction**
    (Structured Glimpse), to send each follow-up reply.

    Args:
        response: Your answer to Thriya's question.
        user_id: Override default user ID.
    
- **thriya_continue_execution**: Continue execution after a phase review pause. Starts the next phase of tasks.

    Args:
        execution_id: The execution ID.
    
- **thriya_create_coherence_policy**: Create a coherence policy that Operate injects into governance checks.

    Args:
        name: Short policy name.
        policy_text: The rule or constraint to apply during coherence checks.
        system_id: Optional stream ID if this should apply only to one stream.
        scope: user, system, entity, or organization.
        priority: Higher numbers are considered first.
        enabled: Whether the policy is active.
        metadata_json: Optional JSON object with policy metadata.

- **thriya_import_perspective_from_chat_content**: Turn RAW conversations / transcripts / posts into a perspective.

    Use this when the thinking is IMPLICIT in behavior rather than written as
    instructions: chat conversations, meeting transcripts, discussions, comment
    threads, email chains, social-media posts, essays, or podcast transcripts.
    Thriya detects the thinker(s), extracts the reasoning patterns — not opinions,
    but HOW they think — and composes a full perspective (briefing, cognitive
    frames, stances) deepened with frontier-model (Opus / GPT-5.5) reasoning.
    The raw text is also ingested as retrievable knowledge.

    NOT for an already-written prompt, system instruction, SOP, or Gem — that is
    explicit instruction text. Use `thriya_import_perspective_from_prompt` for those.

    If multiple thinkers are detected (e.g. in a discussion), you'll be asked
    to choose which one to create. Call again with selected_thinker_index.

    Args:
        content: The raw conversation/transcript/post text (NOT a written prompt/SOP).
        label: Optional label for the content source (e.g. "Naval Ravikant tweets").
        workspace_id: Optional workspace to scope this perspective to.
        selected_thinker_index: If multiple thinkers detected, select one (0-based). Use -1 for auto.
    
- **thriya_import_perspective_from_prompt**: Turn an ALREADY-WRITTEN prompt / SOP / instruction set into a perspective.

    Use this when the thinking is already articulated as explicit instructions:
    Claude/ChatGPT/Gemini custom instructions or system prompts, GPT Actions,
    Gemini Gems, reasoning frameworks, SOPs, or expert how-to notes. Thriya parses
    the instructions into reference frames, then deepens them with frontier-model
    (Opus / GPT-5.5) reasoning to produce a full, composed perspective. If the
    source contains repeatable task instructions, the perspective also gains
    executable expertise that Operate can assign to tasks.

    NOT for raw multi-speaker conversations, transcripts, discussions, tweet dumps,
    email chains, or meeting notes — that material has its reasoning IMPLICIT in
    behavior. Use `thriya_import_perspective_from_chat_content` for those.

    Args:
        raw_text: The already-written prompt / instruction / SOP text.
        name: Override the auto-suggested name (optional).
        description: Override the auto-suggested description (optional).
        user_id: Override default user ID.

- **thriya_list_stances**: List your stance cards -- each captures your reasoning DNA on a topic.

    Args:
        user_id: Override default user ID.
    
- **thriya_list_workspaces**: List all your workspaces.

    Workspaces are intention-scoped environments that group all Thriya tools
    (Operate, Crucible, Perspectives, etc.) under one purpose with domain-specific
    personalization. Each workspace has its own vocabulary, tone, and proactive patterns.

    Returns workspace list with names, intentions, and domain context summaries.
    
- **thriya_mirror_inspiration**: Mirror an inspiration against your accumulated intelligence.

    Instead of just saving content, this reads it THROUGH THE LENS of everything
    Thriya knows about you — your north stars, stances, decisions, learned rules,
    perspectives, and what past mirrors revealed.

    Returns what resonates with your existing thinking, what challenges it,
    what's genuinely new territory, and concrete next steps.

    The mirror is workspace-scoped: if the inspiration belongs to a workspace,
    it mirrors against that workspace's intelligence.

    Args:
        inspiration_id: The inspiration to mirror (from your inspirations list).
    
- **thriya_my_intelligence**: Get your intelligence profile summary.

    Args:
        user_id: Override default user ID.
    
- **thriya_operate_accept_decision**: Crystallize, then accept the endorsed decision from a thinking session.

    For a multi-round deliberation, do NOT simply accept the latest answer — the
    understanding evolved across rounds. First distill one clean decision with
    thriya_operate_crystallize_decision (or have the user author one), then pass that text
    here as `decision`. The endorsed decision becomes the canonical accepted record and the
    full Q&A is preserved as its provenance. For a single-round decision whose answer is
    already clear, you may accept with no override.

    Acceptance is a strong signal that feeds doctrine formation.

    Args:
        session_id: The session_id from the thinking response.
        decision: The crystallized or user-authored decision to lock in. Recommended for any
            multi-round thread. Omit to accept the latest answer as-is.
        reasoning: Optional reasoning behind the decision.
        monitor_next: Optional signals to watch next.
        escalate_when: Optional conditions that would force a rethink.
    
- **thriya_operate_active_session**: Check if you have an in-progress stream onboarding conversation.

    Returns the full chat state (messages, context readiness) if one exists.
    Use this to resume an interrupted onboarding session.
    
- **thriya_operate_add_decision_note**: Add a timestamped note to a saved decision.

    Notes are stored inside the decision artifact and automatically
    feed into the decision memory perspective on next synthesis.
    Attach files (PDFs, images, docs) — text is extracted and feeds into
    doctrine extraction and perspective distillation.

    Args:
        artifact_id: The artifact_id from the decision trajectory
        text: The note text (optional if attachments provided)
        attachments: List of attachment objects [{name, type, size, media_id, url}]. Upload files first via /media/upload.
    
- **thriya_operate_add_outcome_note**: Add a timestamped note to a decision outcome.

    Useful for post-mortem analysis, tracking how an outcome evolved,
    or attaching evidence after the fact. Attach files (PDFs, images, docs) —
    text is extracted and feeds into doctrine extraction and perspective distillation.

    Args:
        outcome_id: The outcome_id from the decision trajectory
        text: The note text (optional if attachments provided)
        attachments: List of attachment objects [{name, type, size, media_id, url}]. Upload files first via /media/upload.
    
- **thriya_operate_add_team_member**: Add an existing workspace member to an organisational team.
- **thriya_operate_adopt_lever**: Adopt an operating lever (from a stream insight report) as a governed doctrine rule.

    The action becomes operating doctrine, guarded by its approval condition; the
    outcome_metric + horizon are recorded so the rule's effect can be checked later.
    status: 'candidate' (default, routes through review) or 'accepted'. Accepting
    workspace doctrine requires admin.
- **thriya_operate_approve_workflow_proposal**: Approve a reviewed workflow proposal and make it the active stream model.

    This changes entity types, relationships, tasks, reports, outcome fields, or
    governance rules and aligns document extraction to the approved vocabulary.
    Call only after the user has seen the proposal diff and explicitly approved it.

    Args:
        proposal_id: Proposal id returned by thriya_operate_workflow_proposals.
        review_note: Optional reason or confirmation recorded in the audit trail.
    
- **thriya_operate_ask_across_streams**: Ask a read-only question across all Operate streams the caller may view.

    The server applies workspace membership and site/scope visibility before any
    stream data reaches the reasoning model. Use this for portfolio-wide or
    corporate questions. Do not use it to write operational data because a
    cross-stream write has no unambiguous destination.

    Args:
        question: The cross-stream question.
        workspace_id: Optional workspace restriction. Omit to search every
            accessible personal and workspace stream.
    
- **thriya_operate_assign_org_role**: Assign an organisational role to exactly one workspace person or team.
- **thriya_operate_bulk_import_commit**: Commit imported decisions as resolved outcomes in a decision stream.

    Call this after preview (and optionally sharpening) to save all extracted
    decisions. Each becomes a resolved outcome ready for doctrine extraction.

    Args:
        import_id: The import_id from thriya_operate_bulk_import_preview.
        system_id: Target decision stream ID.
    
- **thriya_operate_bulk_import_discard**: Discard an in-progress bulk import session.

    Use this when the user wants to abandon an import they started earlier.

    Args:
        import_id: The import_id to discard.
    
- **thriya_operate_bulk_import_pending**: List any in-progress bulk import sessions for the current user.

    Use this to check if there's an unfinished import the user can resume
    (e.g. they started uploading data and left mid-sharpening chat).
    Returns session details including import_id, filename, decision count,
    and how many sharpening questions were answered.

    If a session exists, use thriya_operate_bulk_import_resume to pick up
    where the user left off.
    
- **thriya_operate_bulk_import_preview**: Upload historical decisions for bulk import into an Operate stream.

    Accepts ANY format: CSV, plain text, markdown, or a previously uploaded
    file (PDF, image, docx) via media_id. The system auto-detects whether
    the content is structured (CSV) or unstructured (text/document) and
    extracts decisions accordingly.

    After preview, use thriya_operate_bulk_import_sharpen to extract the
    reasoning framework, then thriya_operate_bulk_import_commit to save.

    Args:
        system_id: Target decision stream ID.
        raw_text: Raw text content (CSV, markdown, plain text, etc.).
        media_id: ID of a previously uploaded file (use thriya_upload_media first for PDF/image/docx).
        filename: Original filename — helps detect format (e.g. "trades.csv", "notes.pdf").
    
- **thriya_operate_bulk_import_resume**: Resume an in-progress bulk import session.

    Restores the full sharpening chat history so the conversation can continue
    from where it left off. Returns the chat so far and the next step.

    Args:
        import_id: The import_id from thriya_operate_bulk_import_pending.
    
- **thriya_operate_bulk_import_sharpen**: Sharpening chat — extract the reasoning framework behind imported decisions.

    Call with empty message to start. The system asks probing questions about
    WHY decisions were made (not just what happened). Reply with your answers.
    After 3-5 turns, the system synthesizes a reasoning context that enriches
    every imported decision.

    This step is optional but strongly recommended — without it, extracted
    rules will be shallow (what happened) rather than actionable (why it happened).

    Args:
        import_id: The import_id from thriya_operate_bulk_import_preview.
        message: Your response to the previous question (empty to start).
    
- **thriya_operate_chat**: Continue a stream onboarding conversation.

    Answer Thriya's questions about your decision domain. After 3-4 exchanges,
    the system will have enough context to generate a domain summary.

    Args:
        chat_id: The chat session ID from thriya_operate_setup.
        message: Your response to Thriya's question.
    
- **thriya_operate_complete_session**: Mark the current onboarding session as complete and clear it.

    Use this if you want to abandon an in-progress onboarding without saving context,
    or after manually saving context via thriya_operate_save_context.
    
- **thriya_operate_compliance_activate_pack**: Activate a compliance pack so its obligations start being tracked and surfaced.
- **thriya_operate_compliance_add_evidence**: Attach structured evidence to an obligation and satisfy it when complete.
- **thriya_operate_compliance_create_pack**: Create a compliance rule pack (a set of obligations for a jurisdiction/sector).

- **thriya_operate_compliance_decide_proposal**: Approve or reject a rule-change proposal — the human-in-the-loop gate on

- **thriya_operate_compliance_nudges**: Generate and list compliance reminders within the caller's visible scopes.
- **thriya_operate_compliance_obligation_status**: Update an obligation's status (e.g. satisfied, in_progress, waived, not_applicable)
    without attaching evidence. Use thriya_operate_compliance_add_evidence to satisfy

- **thriya_operate_compliance_proposals**: List reviewed rule-change proposals for a compliance pack — regulation updates
    awaiting human approval. Approve/reject with thriya_operate_compliance_decide_proposal.
- **thriya_operate_compliance_readiness**: List compliance obligations visible to the caller and their current status.
- **thriya_operate_compliance_trigger**: Create date-versioned compliance obligations for an entity lifecycle event.

    Use after events such as tenant_moved_in, tenant_moved_out, inspection, or
    certificate_recorded. The entity's workspace and scope determine access.
    
- **thriya_operate_consent_status**: Check whether the user has given GDPR consent for Operate data storage.
- **thriya_operate_coordinate**: Create an auditable @mention, task, approval, note, or escalation.

- **thriya_operate_coordination_items**: List assignments, approvals, notes, and escalations in a workspace/stream.
- **thriya_operate_create_entity**: Create a tracked entity in an Operate stream.

    Args:
        system_id: Operate stream id/name.
        name: Entity name.
        entity_type: Domain type, e.g. flat, tenant, campaign, property, trade.

- **thriya_operate_create_entity_link**: Link two entities in an Operate stream hierarchy/map.

        system_id: Operate stream id/name.

- **thriya_operate_create_org_role**: Create an organisational job/function role, separate from access permissions.
- **thriya_operate_create_org_team**: Create an organisational team that can own work, approvals, and escalation.
- **thriya_operate_crystallize_decision**: Distill ONE clean, final decision from a multi-round Operate deliberation.

    After several rounds of Q&A the understanding has shifted, been qualified, maybe partly
    reversed — the latest answer is NOT necessarily the decision. This reads the WHOLE thread
    and proposes a single, unambiguous decision (plus reasoning, what to monitor, and when to
    escalate). It does NOT accept anything.

    Review the proposal, then lock it in by passing its text to
    thriya_operate_accept_decision(session_id, decision=...), or have the user author their
    own. To keep deliberating instead, continue with
    quick_think(session_id=..., operational_context=...).

    Args:
        session_id: The session_id from the thinking response.
    
- **thriya_operate_delete_decision**: Delete a single decision and its associated outcome.

    This is destructive — the decision and outcome are permanently removed.
    Perspectives retain any patterns already learned from this decision.

    Args:
        artifact_id: The artifact_id from the decision trajectory
    
- **thriya_operate_delete_decision_note**: Delete a note from a decision by its index (0-based).

    Args:
        artifact_id: The artifact_id from the decision trajectory
        note_index: Zero-based index of the note to delete

    Args:
        entity_id: Entity id from `thriya_operate_entities`.
    
- **thriya_operate_delete_entity_link**: Delete an entity relationship/link.

    Args:
        link_id: Link id from `thriya_operate_entity_links`.
    
- **thriya_operate_delete_outcome_note**: Delete a note from an outcome by its index (0-based).

    Args:
        outcome_id: The outcome_id from the decision trajectory
        note_index: Zero-based index of the note to delete
    
- **thriya_operate_delete_stream**: Delete all decisions, outcomes, and doctrine in a stream.

    This is a destructive operation — it cascades through artifacts,

    Also refreshes the decision memory perspective.

    Args:
        system_id: The decision stream to delete
    
- **thriya_operate_detect_pii**: Detect names and identifiers (PII) in text before it goes to an LLM.

    Uses local NER — no data leaves the server. Returns detected entities
    with positions so the user can review and clean the text.

    Args:
        text: The text to scan for PII
    
- **thriya_operate_directory**: List workspace people, teams, job roles, and valid @mention targets.

    Workspace access roles (owner/admin/member/viewer) are returned separately
    from organisational roles such as Compliance Officer or Regional Manager.

    Args:

        system_id: Optional Operate stream id. When provided, results are filtered

- **thriya_operate_discovery**: Start an Operate-level discovery conversation before any stream is known.

    Use this when the user asks where Operate could help them, their team, or their
    organisation, or when they are unsure what stream(s) to create. This is above
    any single stream: it interviews the user, finds recurring operational loops,
    then recommends one or more candidate streams with benefits, execution hands,

    Args:
        initial_context: Optional description of the person, team, company, pains, or processes.
    
- **thriya_operate_distill_stream**: Distill a stream's learned rules into a shareable perspective.

    Creates a standalone AI Perspective from the accepted learned rules in this stream.
    Recipients get the distilled intelligence — patterns, lessons, rules — without
    seeing the user's private decisions.

    Args:
        system_id: The stream to distill (e.g., "forex-trading").
        name: Name for the perspective (defaults to "<stream> Intelligence").
        visibility: "shared" (invite-only), "open" (anyone on Thriya), or "private".

    Returns:
        The new perspective details, or an error if no intelligence to distill.
    
- **thriya_operate_entities**: List the living entities tracked inside an Operate stream.

    Entities are the stream's operating objects: flats, customers, campaigns,
    trades, candidates, projects, assets, or any other domain-specific thing.

    Args:
        system_id: Operate stream id/name.
        entity_type: Optional filter, e.g. flat, customer, campaign.
        include_tree: Include hierarchy/tree view.
        workspace_id: Optional workspace. Rows are filtered to scopes the caller
            is permitted to view.
    
- **thriya_operate_entity_intelligence**: Read one entity's accumulated intelligence inside its Operate stream.

    Two distinct layers, kept separate:
    - LEARNED JUDGMENT: reasoning patterns earned from THIS entity's resolved
      outcomes (how it tends to behave, what to weight or discount). Empty until
      the entity has crossed the resolved-outcome threshold — thin entities have none.
    - MEMORY (data): the entity's hierarchy, recent activity/events, resolved
      outcomes, and linked entities, retrieved live (not baked into judgment).

    Use this to reason WITH an entity's own history rather than from scratch.

    Args:
        entity_id: The entity whose intelligence to read.
    
- **thriya_operate_entity_links**: List links for one Operate entity.

    Args:
        entity_id: Entity id.
        system_id: Operate stream id/name.
    
- **thriya_operate_external_announcement**: Send a general announcement to everyone connected to a customer portal.

    Args:
        portal_id: Portal id from `thriya_operate_external_portals`.
        title: Announcement title.
        message: Announcement body.
        expires_at: Optional ISO timestamp.

    Use this before replying to a customer/client/tenant. It analyzes the case

    thriya_operate_external_case_update only after the user approves the reply.

    Args:

        urgency: Optional urgency: low, normal, urgent, emergency.
        message_to_customer: Optional public update visible to the submitter.
        staff_notes: Optional internal note.
        compliance_flags_json: Optional JSON array of compliance flags.
    
- **thriya_operate_external_cases**: List customer/client/tenant cases submitted into an Operate stream.

    Args:
        system_id: Operate stream id/name.
        status: Optional status filter such as new, triaging, in_progress,

- **thriya_operate_external_dashboard**: View management-level summary for external cases in an Operate stream.

    Shows open cases, urgency mix, compliance-sensitive count, repeat locations
    or customers, and recent cases. Use this for portfolio/customer operations
    oversight, not for public participant access.

    Args:
        system_id: Operate stream id/name.
    
- **thriya_operate_external_portal**: Create or fetch a public customer/client/tenant portal for an Operate stream.

    Use this when external participants should submit and track only their own
    cases while staff and managers keep the full Operate stream private. The

    Args:
        system_id: Operate stream id/name.
        workspace_id: Optional workspace id.
        industry_template: Template id, e.g. property_management_uk or generic.
        label: Optional portal label.
